output.reason: A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot cut now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection today (probing for depth/abscess, pulse and sensation check, possible cultures/imaging), which a messaging-only plan cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please get your foot looked at in person today — urgent care, your doctor, or a foot/diabetes clinic. In diabetes, a cut with spreading redness, swelling and tenderness can be an infection that needs the wound examined, checked for depth or pus, and treatment started. Keep weight off that foot. If you develop fever, chills, spreading redness, streaking, drainage, or black or foul-smelling skin, go to an emergency department right away.
differential: Cellulitis/local wound infection of a diabetic foot ulcer
Deeper infection such as abscess or involvement of underlying tissue/bone

redFlags.concern: Wound with surrounding erythema, swelling and tenderness
redFlags.quote: the skin around it is red and a little swollen

redFlags.concern: Purulent drainage, black tissue or foul odor

output.vitalSigns: No vital sign values reported; patient states "No fever" but no temperature reading, heart rate or blood glucose was given and whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Only consumer-level diabetic foot summaries and an ED cellulitis synthesis are available; neither provides telehealth triage thresholds for this unexamined patient.

citations.claim: Consumer diabetes guidance advises prompt clinician assessment for red, warm or painful skin on the feet.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; does not specify setting, timing interval or need for imaging.

citations.claim: Serious diabetic foot problems can develop quickly, supporting same-day rather than deferred assessment.
citations.limitation: General statement, not individualized risk stratification.
